questions.question: Which of the following countries hosted the 16th G20 Summit in 2021?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Italy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **16th**** G20 Summit in October 2021 **was hosted by **Italy in the city of Rome.**
 
• The summit focussed on three broad, interconnected pillars of action: **People, Planet, and Prosperity**.
 
• **Prime Minister Narendra Modi **took part in the summit.
 
• ​​At the summit, the leaders committed to the **key Paris Agreement goal of limiting global warming to 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **G20 Summit of 2022 and 2023 **will be hosted by **Indonesia and India respectively**.
 
• The G20 is a **strategic multilateral platform connecting the world's major developed and emerging economies **which holds a strategic role in securing future global economic growth and prosperity.
 
• It consists of **19 countries and European Union**.
 
• It was established in **1999 and headquartered in Mexico**.
 
• **Joko Widodo **is the current chairman of the G20.
 
• ** Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Republic of Korea, Mexico, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Turkey, the United Kingdom, the United States, and the European Union **are the members of G20.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• ** 2023**
 
• India hosted the 2023 G20 summit, with the theme "One Earth, One Family, One Future". The summit was chaired by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and India's presidency began on December 1, 2022. India's priorities included green development, climate finance, and accelerated growth. 
 
• **2024**
 
• Brazil will host the 2024 G20 summit, with the presidency beginning on December 1, 2023 and ending on November 30, 2024. The summit will be held in Rio de Janeiro.

questions.question: The marks of furrows were discovered at the Harappan site in ________.

__
 
• The marks of furrows were discovered in the** Kalibangan site of Indus valley currently Rajasthan.**

• **Dholavira-** The site of the Indus valley civilisation is considered to be the **second largest Harappan site in India and the fifth largest in the Indian subcontinent.**
 
• **Bhansali- **It was the** Harappan site currently located in Fatehabad district Haryana.** Beads** **of semi-precious stones, **terracotta, steatite and bangles of clay, shell, faience and copper **are some of the findings on this site.

questions.question: Robert Hooke discovered the cell in 1665 by observing a ________ under a microscope.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**piece of cork**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Cell** was discovered by **Robert Hooke in 1665 **by observing a **piece of cork under a microscope**.
 
• In his observation, he saw **tiny boxlike cavities termed Cells**.
 
• He described his detailed observation in his book **Micrographia **as an exploration of a **tiny unseen world.**
 
• His discovery opened a new dimension of knowledge and exploration to the smallest unit of life **The Cell**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Cell **is the **fundamental structural and functional unit of all living organisms**.
 
• After Robert Hooke a **dutch scientist Antonie van Leeuwenhoek **discoverd other hidden microorganisms **Bacteria and Protozoa**.
 
• The classical cell theory was given by **Theodor Schwann in 1839 and had three parts.**
 
 
• **​All living organisms are made up of cells.**
 
• **Cells are basic units of life.**
 
• **Cells come from pre-existing cells**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of food and water contamination?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bites by stray animals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bites by stray animals do not cause **food and water contamination**, 
 
• **Food and water contamination** infects them with toxins and harmful chemicals which cause severe diseases such as diarrhoea, dysentery, and food poisoning.
 
• Food contamination results in the** development of bacteria, parasites, and other micro-organisms** which **enter our body and disturb our metabolism and other functioning.**
 
• **Chemical contamination of food and water **can even lead to **acute poisoning or long-term diseases, such as cancer.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Chemical runoff from factories **ultimately drains out into our water bodies which are the major source of water for man,** the waste from factories contaminates our water bodies which affect human as well as animal life.
 
• Incorrect food storage leads to the **spoilage of food at a faster rate**.
 
• Infectious organisms in the atmosphere occur because of different types of pollution like **emission of toxic gases, usage of chemical fertilizers etc it directly or indirectly affects our natural resources like contamination of water bodies, fertility of the soil, these adverse effects results in contamination of food and water at different levels.**

questions.question: What do you call the process of change in the base pair sequence of an organism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mutation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of change in the base pair sequence of an organism is called **Mutation.**
 
• Mutation refers to the **abnormality in the genetic sequence of an organism**.
 
• The mutation results in an **alteration In the composition of DNA.**
 
• It leads to variation in the normal **characteristics of an organism, these variations can have negative or positive effects on the organism**.
 
• It is a **heritable change and can also affect the offspring**.
 
• Geneticist **Hugo de Vries **coined the term **Mutation in 1901**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decantation-** The process of removing liquid components from a mixture having solid or other immiscible substances.
 
• **Pollination- **Process or transfer of pollen grains from anther to stigma.
 
• **Ionisation- **Process by which any atom acquires positive or negative charge by gaining or losing of electrons.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an age-verification test method that makes an assessment based on hand and wrist radiographs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The cervical vertebral maturation method**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **cervical vertebral maturation method**** (CVM)** method is used to t**rack the growth of skeletal maturation at a particular point in time**.
 
• Along with evolving technology, **various methods of age calculation have been developed using different elements and visualization techniques like ultrasound, x-ray etc.**
 
• Bone age assessment based on hand and wrist radiographs is **one of the most preferred techniques of getting information about bone age**.
 
• Various methods have been developed **now days to compute bone age scores from radiographs by comparing the maturity of hand & wrist bones.**
 
• Some of them are ** Greulich & Pyle (GP) Atlas, Tanner Whitehouse (TW2) Method, The Gilsanz & Ratibin (GR) Atlas, Automatic Skeletal Bone Age Assessment etc.****​​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **The Greulich-Pyle method- It i**s an integrated method based on “**The Radiographic Atlas of Skeletal Development of the Hand and Wrist”, by Dr William Walter Greulich and Dr Sarah Idell Pyle,** which was** last published in 1**959, but still one of the most commonly used atlas for bone age measurement by radiologists in western countries.
 
• **The Tanner-Whitehouse method- **The Tanner-Whitehouse II method is a **bone-specific scoring technique in which a numerical score is assigned to selected hand-wrist bones **depending on the appearance of certain well-defined maturity indicators.
 
• **The FELS method of** assessing the skeletal maturity of the hand wrist involves th**e provision of a range of shapes to which maturity indicator grades **which can be assigned and in the **statistical methods used to construct the scale of skeletal maturity.**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a service provided to its clients by banks in India?
questions.solution:
The current answer is __**URL**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **URL **is NOT a service provided to its clients by banks in India.
 
• URL stands for **Uniform Resource Locator it is a kind of link or unique address which specifies the location of a file or data present on the web.**
 
• In simple language, URL is the address which we enter in our web browser to go to a particular site like** www.testbook.com**.
 
• **NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, ECS, and Credit Cards** are some of the services provided by the banks to the customers.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NEFT- **Stands for **National Electronic Funds Transfer and **is a kind of **electronic fund transfer** service provided by banks to customers to transfer thei**r money all over the country.** It was first started in** November 2005.**
 
• **RTGS- Real-time gross settlement **is a special type of funds transfer system which enables the transfer of money or securities between one bank to any other bank on a real-time and gross basis. **Large funds transfers take place under this service. The minimum limit for this service is 2 lakh rupees**.
 
• **ECS- which stands for Electronic Clearance Service **is a mode of payment which is **used in the type of transactions that are repetitive in nature for example salary, pension, premium, and dividend.**
